welcome_message:
SDP Expectation Notifications: Asset Installer

Installs two things that ship together:
  1. A reference Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipeline demonstrating
     per-expectation data-quality notification: a native event hook fires the
     moment a WARN expectation result is logged, on the public
     samples.nyctaxi.trips dataset (the worked example).
  2. A companion agent skill that instructs a coding agent to wire the same
     hook-plus-backstop pattern into YOUR own SDP pipeline.

The pattern is a pair, not a single mechanism: event hook delivery is
explicitly best-effort (the platform does not guarantee every hook runs
before pipeline compute terminates), so the asset also installs exactly one
DABs-managed Alert v2 that sweeps the published pipeline event log on a
schedule as the guaranteed path. Hook = fast, alert = guaranteed.

The hook is throttled by design: without it, one failing expectation
notifies once per microbatch (measured live), which floods on multi-batch
and continuous pipelines. A time-aware two-layer throttle (in-memory always,
durable volume markers optionally) caps it at one notification per
expectation per window.

The demo WARN expectation is a deliberate tripwire chosen to fail on the
healthy public sample, so the hook fires and the backstop alert triggers on
the first run with no extra setup.

Let's pick the install settings...

target_dir.description:
Target directory for the pipeline source files (relative to your bundle root).
The asset installs the pipeline source (with the event hook) and the
event-log parsing queries here. Pick a path that doesn't already exist.
target_dir
target_dir.pattern_match_failure_message: Target directory must start with a letter, number, or underscore and contain only letters, numbers, underscores, slashes, hyphens, or dots.

pipeline_resource_key.description:
========================================

DABs resource key for the pipeline.

This key appears in the bundle as `resources.pipelines.<key>` and is also the
filename: `resources/<key>.pipeline.yml`. The backstop alert resource is
named after it too: `resources/<key>_backstop.alert.yml` with key
`<key>_backstop`.

Default `sdp_expectation_notifications` is safe for most projects. Pick
another name only if your bundle already defines a pipeline with this key.
Must be lowercase snake_case (letters, numbers, underscores).
pipeline_resource_key
pipeline_resource_key.pattern_match_failure_message: Resource key must be lowercase, start with a letter, and contain only letters, numbers, and underscores.

pipeline_name.description:
========================================

Display name shown in the Databricks workspace Pipelines list.
Free-form; spaces and mixed case are fine.
pipeline_name

catalog.description:
========================================

Unity Catalog catalog the pipeline writes its table and event log into.

You need CREATE TABLE on this catalog and on the schema below. The public
source (samples.nyctaxi.trips) is read-only and unaffected.
Must be a valid lowercase identifier.
catalog
catalog.pattern_match_failure_message: Catalog must be lowercase, start with a letter, and contain only letters, numbers, and underscores.

schema.description:
========================================

Unity Catalog schema for the demo table and the published pipeline event log
(the table the backstop alert queries). Created by the pipeline if missing,
provided you have CREATE SCHEMA on the catalog.
Must be a valid lowercase identifier.
schema
schema.pattern_match_failure_message: Schema must be lowercase, start with a letter, and contain only letters, numbers, and underscores.

warehouse_id.description:
========================================

SQL warehouse id the backstop alert runs its sweep query on.

Find yours with: databricks warehouses list
If you installed the `monitoring-sql-warehouse` asset from this same repo
(a 2X-Small serverless warehouse with auto_stop_mins=1, built exactly for
this workload shape), you can reference it instead:
  ${resources.sql_warehouses.monitoring_sql_warehouse.id}

Keep the default placeholder to defer the choice; replace it in
resources/<pipeline_resource_key>_backstop.alert.yml before deploying.
warehouse_id
warehouse_id.pattern_match_failure_message: Warehouse id cannot be empty or contain whitespace.

notification_email.description:
========================================

Email address the backstop alert notifies when the sweep finds expectation
violations. Must belong to a user in the workspace.

Keep the default placeholder to defer the choice; replace it in
resources/<pipeline_resource_key>_backstop.alert.yml before deploying.
notification_email
notification_email.pattern_match_failure_message: Notification email cannot be empty or contain whitespace.

state_volume_path.description:
========================================

Path under an EXISTING Unity Catalog volume where the hook keeps its
notification throttle state, for example /Volumes/main/dq_notifications/state.
Marker files land in <path>/dq_notify_state/<pipeline>/, one small JSON per
monitored expectation, overwritten in place (the folder never grows).

The asset deliberately does not create or manage a volume; state that
describes operations should outlive any one bundle.

Keep the default placeholder to run with the in-memory throttle only (still
removes per-microbatch repeats within an update); set the path later in
resources/<pipeline_resource_key>.pipeline.yml (dq_notify.state_dir) to add
cross-update throttling.
state_volume_path
state_volume_path.pattern_match_failure_message: Volume path cannot be empty or contain whitespace.

skill_dir.description:
========================================

Target directory for the companion agent skill (relative to your bundle root).
The skill installs at <skill_dir>/skills/sdp-expectation-notifications/ and
instructs a coding agent to wire the hook-plus-backstop pattern into your own
SDP pipeline.

Default `.agents` is vendor-neutral. If you use one agent and want
auto-discovery, override with its native folder:
  - Claude Code:  .claude
  - Codex:        .codex
  - Cursor:       .cursor
  - Gemini CLI:   .gemini

Pick a path whose `skills/sdp-expectation-notifications/` subfolder doesn't
already exist in your project.
skill_dir
skill_dir.pattern_match_failure_message: Skill directory must start with a letter, number, underscore, or dot and contain only letters, numbers, underscores, slashes, hyphens, or dots.

success_message:
========================================

Expectation notifications installed (reference pipeline + backstop alert + companion skill):
  - Pipeline source: {{.target_dir}}/expectation_notifications_pipeline.py (event hook inside)
  - Event log SQL:   {{.target_dir}}/event_log_queries.sql
  - Pipeline:        resources/{{.pipeline_resource_key}}.pipeline.yml
  - Backstop alert:  resources/{{.pipeline_resource_key}}_backstop.alert.yml
  - Usage doc:       docs/sdp-expectation-notifications/README.md
  - Agent skill:     {{.skill_dir}}/skills/sdp-expectation-notifications/SKILL.md

Run the reference as-is:

1. Confirm your `databricks.yml` includes the resource files. Most bundles
   already include `resources/*.yml` by default; verify:
     include:
       - resources/*.yml

2. If you kept a placeholder for the warehouse id or the notification email,
   replace it in resources/{{.pipeline_resource_key}}_backstop.alert.yml.
   If you kept the volume-path placeholder, the throttle runs in-memory only;
   set dq_notify.state_dir in resources/{{.pipeline_resource_key}}.pipeline.yml
   later to add cross-update throttling. For a real webhook, put the URL in a
   secret scope (it is a credential):
     databricks secrets create-scope dq-notifications
     databricks secrets put-secret dq-notifications slack_webhook_url --string-value "<url>"
   then set dq_notify.webhook_secret_scope: dq-notifications in the pipeline
   configuration.

3. Validate, deploy, run:
     databricks bundle validate -t <your-target>
     databricks bundle deploy -t <your-target>
     databricks bundle run {{.pipeline_resource_key}} -t <your-target>

4. The demo WARN expectation fails on the healthy public sample by design, so
   the hook prints its notification during the first update (visible in the
   pipeline compute's driver log) and the backstop alert triggers on its next
   scheduled sweep (daily 06:00 UTC by default; open the alert in the UI and
   run it manually to see it immediately).

The demo table lands at {{.catalog}}.{{.schema}}.monitored_trips; the event
log publishes to {{.catalog}}.{{.schema}}.dq_notifications_event_log. Inspect
per-expectation counts with {{.target_dir}}/event_log_queries.sql. Design
notes and the honest caveats (hook delivery is best-effort; that is why the
backstop exists) live in 'docs/sdp-expectation-notifications/README.md'.

Wire the pattern into YOUR pipeline with the companion skill:

  Point your coding agent at the skill and ask it to add the hook-plus-backstop
  pattern to your own SDP pipeline. Wire it the way your agent expects:
    - Claude Code: auto-discovered if {{.skill_dir}} is `.claude`; otherwise
      add to CLAUDE.md: 'Use the skill at
      {{.skill_dir}}/skills/sdp-expectation-notifications/SKILL.md'.
    - Codex: reference that SKILL.md path from AGENTS.md.
    - Other / on Databricks (Genie): point the agent at the SKILL.md path.

  A ready-to-paste kickoff prompt is in 'docs/sdp-expectation-notifications/README.md'.
